title: Working-Memory Load Laboratory
summary: Hold two, four or six items in mind while doing something else. Compare what it costs when the something else is in the same domain as the material and when it is not.
learningObjectives: Read a load function and describe it as a curve rather than a fixed number of slots.
Explain why a same-domain concurrent task costs more than a different-domain one of equal pacing.
Distinguish storage load, attentional control and task similarity as explanations.
Identify findings that a design of this kind cannot speak to.
Explain the difference between operationalising a demand and measuring a capacity.
interactionTypes: paced concurrent judgements in a fixed retention interval
seeded simulated class dataset covering all four combinations
line chart paired with a data table
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; responses stay in the browser tab as JavaScript variables and disappear on reload, and nothing is written to storage.
accessibilityNotes: The display changes at most once every 1.8 seconds and only its contents change; the panel, its size and its position stay put. Nothing fades, moves or animates and no CSS animation or transition is used anywhere, so there is nothing for a reduced-motion setting to switch off. Only the concurrent judgements are paced, and they are paced deliberately so that the retention interval is the same length in every condition, including the do-nothing baseline; the recognition probe is never timed out and the worked example reaches every conclusion without running a trial. Nothing depends on colour: filled grid cells differ from empty ones in fill and the probed cell is marked by a thick dashed ring as well, the symmetry pattern is drawn in the text colour with a dashed mirror line, and chart points are squares carrying their own printed percentage. The trial display is aria-hidden because reading it aloud would be the answer. Response buttons are rebuilt for each phase with their answer written in words and are at least 3.25rem tall. The chart is aria-hidden and paired inside the same figure with a five-column table. Every control has an accessible name, headings do not skip, focus moves to the results heading and to the first response button of each phase, and forced-colours rules are supplied for the display, the grid, the pattern and the chart. Usable at 320px and at projector widths with no horizontal page scroll; wide tables scroll inside their own containers.
readmeTopic: Working-memory load: storage, control and similarity are three different things
simulationNotes: The learner's own trials are real responses, not simulated. A trial is 2500 ms of encoding, a retention interval of three judgements at a fixed 1800 ms each (or an equal blank wait in the do-nothing condition), and one untimed recognition probe with a 50 per cent chance of being in the set. Holding decay time constant across conditions is the reason the judgements are paced. Loads are 2, 4 and 6 items with four trials each; material is a set of consonants or a set of cells in a 4x4 grid; the concurrent task is a two-syllable judgement on a printed word (verbal) or a left-right symmetry judgement on a pattern (visuospatial). Symmetric patterns are built by mirroring two columns and asymmetric ones by flipping exactly one cell, so the two kinds have the same density on average. Missed judgements are recorded as misses rather than dropped. The worked example is four simulated classes of 100 fictional participants contributing four trials per load each, so 400 observations per cell, with mulberry32 seeds 20260991 to 20260994. Memory accuracy by load is set at 0.95 / 0.80 / 0.66 for letters with syllables, 0.96 / 0.90 / 0.82 for letters with symmetry, 0.94 / 0.79 / 0.64 for positions with symmetry and 0.96 / 0.89 / 0.81 for positions with syllables; concurrent-task accuracy is 0.86 in the same-domain runs and 0.93 in the different-domain runs, and concurrent-task time is 1080 ms or 940 ms plus 30 ms per item held. The values at two items are deliberately equal across runs because there is little to interfere with at that load, and the selective-interference gap opens at four and six. That pattern is built into the generator to illustrate the classic finding; it is not evidence for it, not a norm and not anybody's data. The tool operationalises a demand and says so; it does not estimate working-memory capacity, and it does not manipulate attentional control at all.
